items.note: 还 + predicate + 呢 can echo a claim with disbelief or dismissiveness, or emphasize that a state still holds. It is not a progressive marker; learners often place 呢 after 还 instead of at the end.
来得及 and 来不及 come before a verb phrase to say whether there is enough time before a deadline. Learners sometimes reverse the verb and its object; keep the usual verb–object order after this pattern.

拿 + item + 来说 introduces an example, and the following clause says something about it. Use this pattern to focus discussion on one representative case. Learners may move 拿 or 来说 away from the item, breaking the pattern.

大约 comes before a quantity to show that the figure is approximate. Put the number before its measure word, and the measure word before the noun; for a length, use a measure expression such as 三公里长. Learners may omit or misplace the measure word.

此外 and 另外 introduce a separate point or consideration after an initial clause. Use either to add information rather than to restate the first point. Learners should keep the added point separate and avoid treating these words as part of the preceding clause.

Use 不是 + the first option, followed by 就是 + the second option, to present one of two likely alternatives. Learners may reverse or scramble the markers; keep 不是 with the first option and 就是 with the second.

items.phrase: 他不是开玩笑就是聊天儿
items.zh: 他不是开玩笑，就是聊天儿。
items.en: He is either joking or chatting.
items.wrong: 他就是不是开玩笑，聊天儿。
items.wrongPy: tā jiù shì bú shì kāi wán xiào liáo tiānr
items.why: 不是 must introduce the first option and 就是 the second; the correct order is 他不是开玩笑，就是聊天儿。

items.note: Put 就是了 after the whole verb phrase to reassure someone that doing that is enough. Learners may insert 就是了 inside the verb phrase; keep the action together before 就是了.
Put 按时 before the verb phrase to say that an action happens at its scheduled time. Learners may place it after the verb or between a verb and its object; keep 按时 before the whole action.

不过 introduces a limitation or qualification after the first clause. Keep the second clause’s subject and negation in their usual positions; learners may misplace 不 or move an adverb away from the verb it modifies.

A negative question followed by a predicate can challenge the idea that the situation is acceptable. Use it when context suggests the expected answer is obvious. Learners may mistake it for a neutral question; the rhetorical force comes from the context and the negative wording.

左右 follows a quantity or time expression to mean approximately that amount or duration. 前后 normally approximates a time point. Learners may put 左右 before the quantity, but it belongs after the expression it qualifies.

items.en: Travel for around half a day.
items.wrongPy: lǚ xíng zuǒ yòu bàn tiān
items.why: 左右 must follow the approximate duration; put it after 半天, as in 旅行半天左右.

items.note: 从来 and 从没 express that something has never happened over the relevant period, and 从 must be followed by a negative predicate. Use 不 or 没 before the verb. Learners may put the negation after the verb, but it belongs before it.

items.en: He has never worked a part-time job.
items.wrongPy: tā cóng lái dǎ gōng bù
items.why: 不 must precede 打工; the correct order is 他从来不打工.

items.en: I never sign up.
items.wrongPy: wǒ cóng lái bào míng bù
items.why: 不 must precede 报名; the correct order is 我从来不报名.

items.note: 从来都 comes before the predicate to describe something that has always been true over the relevant history. In affirmative assessments, 都 commonly follows 从来. Learners may put 都 after 很, but it belongs before the predicate’s degree word here.

忽然 goes before a verb phrase to show that an event happens abruptly or unexpectedly. Use it to modify the event, not to describe what happens afterward. Learners may place it at the end of the verb phrase, but it should come before the verb.

items.en: He suddenly made a sound.
items.wrongPy: tā fā chū shēng yīn hū rán
items.why: 忽然 must come before the verb phrase, as in 他忽然发出声音.

items.en: He suddenly fell down.
items.wrongPy: tā diào xià lai le hū rán
items.why: 忽然 must come before the verb phrase, as in 他忽然掉下来了.

items.note: 再也不 + verb phrase means that something will not happen again, while 再也没 + verb phrase describes no further occurrence in a past context. Learners may place 不 after the verb, but it must come before the verb phrase.

items.en: Never get hurt again.
items.wrongPy: zài yě shòu shāng bù
items.why: 不 must precede the verb phrase; the correct order is 再也不受伤.

items.note: 重新 goes immediately before a verb phrase to say that an action is done anew. It can modify a verb with its object, but learners should not place it inside or after that verb phrase, where the intended structure breaks down.

items.en: Enter the restaurant again.
items.wrongPy: jìn rù chóng xīn cān tīng
items.why: 重新 must precede the verb phrase; the correct order is 重新进入餐厅.

items.en: Carry out the activity again.
items.wrongPy: jìn xíng huó dòng chóng xīn
items.why: 重新 cannot follow the verb phrase here; the correct order is 重新进行活动.

items.phrase: 他重新进行活动成功了
items.zh: 他重新进行活动，成功了。
items.en: He carried out the activity again and succeeded.
items.wrong: 他进行活动重新，成功了。
items.wrongPy: tā jìn xíng huó dòng chóng xīn chéng gōng le
items.why: 重新 must precede the verb phrase; the correct order is 他重新进行活动，成功了.

items.note: 把 places the known object before the verb, and the phrase after the verb can quantify the action’s duration or number of repetitions. Learners may choose a noun measure word instead of the action-count expression 一下.
正好 goes before a predicate to say that a circumstance fits or coincides exactly. Learners may put it after the predicate or between a verb and its object, but it should not be placed there.

items.en: The traveler happens to check into the inn.
items.wrongPy: lǚ kè rù zhù zhèng hǎo lǚ guǎn
items.why: 正好 precedes the predicate 入住; say 旅客正好入住旅馆, not 旅客入住正好旅馆.

items.note: Put 赶紧 or 赶快 before the verb phrase to say that an action should happen without delay. A common mistake is placing the adverb inside the verb phrase or inserting 了 after it; keep the adverb before the whole action.

items.en: Quickly sign up for the competition.
items.wrongPy: cān sài bào míng gǎn kuài
items.why: This reverses the action sequence and strands the adverb; put 赶快 before 报名参赛.

items.note: Use 多么 before an adjective to make an exclamation about a high degree, as in “How quiet!” It is not a question asking how much or how; learners often put 多么 after the adjective or after the subject instead of before the adjective.

Put the intentionality adverb before the whole verb phrase to say an action was deliberate. Learners sometimes place it between a verb and its object or inside a compound verb, where it breaks the phrase.
This construction presents a striking case, then uses 都 or 也 before its predicate; a second case is stronger with 更. Learners often misplace 都 after the predicate or before the case.

Use 把 with an object already known in context, then reduplicate the verb to suggest a brief or casual action. Some verbs take 一 before the repeated verb. Learners often put the object after the verb, which breaks the 把 construction.

items.en: Check the answers.
items.wrongPy: bǎ duì dá àn yí duì
items.why: The object must follow 把 and come before the verb; say 把答案对一对。

items.note: Place 按 or 按照 before the rule, order, or standard, then give the action that follows it. Learners may put the rule after the action; keep the standard before the verb phrase.
Use 任何 before a noun to mean any member of a set; 都 then scopes over the whole assertion. Learners often put 都 between 任何 and its noun, breaking the fixed order.
Use verb + number + 顿 to count a bounded bout, such as a scolding; 顿 can also precede a meal noun. Keep the number before 顿—learners often reverse them or use the wrong measure word.
并且 links a first clause to a second, often adding or strengthening an assertion. Put a complete clause after 并且; learners sometimes move a clause's subject or predicate into the wrong order.
既...又/也 presents two compatible properties or actions as a pair. Keep 既 before the first predicate and 又 or 也 before the second; learners often misplace or omit one of these markers.

Put 互相 or 相互 after the plural subject and immediately before a verb that people can do to one another. Use it for reciprocal actions, not merely simultaneous actions. Learners often put the marker after the verb; it belongs before the verb phrase.

Place 并 between two parallel verbs or verb phrases to coordinate compatible actions or descriptions, especially in relatively formal writing. Learners sometimes attach 并 to a noun or put it before the first action; it should link the two predicates.

Use 由 plus the responsible person, then 来, then the action. This pattern assigns who will perform the action. Learners may place 来 after the verb, but here it belongs between the agent and the verb phrase.

Use 自 or 由 before a starting time or place, followed by the verb phrase. This is a relatively formal way to give the source or starting point. Learners often put 自 or 由 after the verb; it must introduce the starting point.

Put 各种 directly before a noun to refer to various kinds of something. It can describe things that are available, discussed, or present somewhere. Learners may split the expression and put 种 after the noun; keep 各种 together before the noun.

In this formal disposal pattern, 将 introduces a known object, which comes before a bounded verb phrase. The action is often marked as completed with 了. Do not confuse this object-marking use with 将 as a future marker before a verb phrase.

十分 goes before a gradable predicate to express a high degree, like “very.” Use it to intensify descriptions or states, not to count ten points. Learners may place it after the predicate; it belongs before the predicate.

在 + a domain + 方面 sets the respect or area to which the following claim applies. Use it at the start of the clause, before the claim. Learners may put 在 after 方面 or confuse the domain phrase with the claim itself.

也许 introduces a proposition as a tentative possibility, rather than a fact. It can appear before the whole proposition or after its subject. Learners may insert it inside a phrase or place 都 after the verb instead of before it.

由于 introduces a cause, and 因此 introduces its result, often in a relatively formal explanation. Use them in that order to link the clauses. Learners may reverse the connectors and accidentally present the result as the cause.

Use 不如 to say that the subject falls short of a comparison target in a stated quality; the target comes after 不如 and the adjective follows the target. The quality can sometimes be understood from context. Learners often put the adjective before the target.

尤其 goes before the predicate to single out something as especially prominent. It can introduce a verb phrase, as in 尤其重视教育, or follow a subject and precede its predicate. Learners may mistakenly place 尤其 after the predicate.

要是 introduces a condition, and 就 introduces its consequence. The condition comes first, followed by the consequence; 吧 may appear at the end as a suggestion. Learners often put 要是 or 就 in the wrong clause or position.

items.en: If there is free time, read novels.
items.wrongPy: yǒu kōng yào shi jiù yuè dú xiǎo shuō
items.why: 要是 must introduce the condition, so say 要是有空，就阅读小说。

items.phrase: 要是有趣就观看电视剧
items.zh: 要是有趣，就观看电视剧。
items.en: If it is interesting, watch the TV drama.
items.wrong: 有趣要是，就观看电视剧。
items.wrongPy: yǒu qù yào shi jiù guān kàn diàn shì jù
items.why: 要是 must introduce the condition, so say 要是有趣，就观看电视剧。

items.phrase: 要是你有空就阅读文章吧
items.zh: 要是你有空，就阅读文章吧。
items.en: If you have free time, read an article.
items.wrong: 要是你有空，就吧阅读文章。
items.wrongPy: yào shi nǐ yǒu kōng jiù ba yuè dú wén zhāng
items.why: 吧 belongs at the end of the suggestion, so say 要是你有空，就阅读文章吧。

items.note: 即使 introduces a conceded or hypothetical condition, and 也 marks the consequence that still holds despite it. Put 也 before the consequence, not inside the condition. Learners often place 也 in the wrong clause.
Use 既然 before a fact the speaker accepts, then 就 before the result or recommendation. Learners often put 就 in the first clause; it belongs with the consequence.
Put 至少 before the amount or minimum requirement, or before the claim that establishes a minimum. Learners often place it after the phrase it limits, which breaks the intended scope.
Use 就是 before the concessive condition and 也 before the consequence to mean “even if ... still ...”. Learners may mistake 就是 for an identifying 是 or place 也 after the subject.

items.en: Even if the distance is great, I’ll still perform.
items.wrongPy: jiù shì jù lí yuǎn yě wǒ yǎn
items.why: 也 belongs before 我演, as in 就是距离远，我也演。

items.phrase: 就是小说很普通我也租
items.zh: 就是小说很普通，我也租。
items.en: Even if the novel is very ordinary, I’ll still rent it.
items.wrong: 就是小说很普通，也我租。
items.wrongPy: jiù shì xiǎo shuō hěn pǔ tōng yě wǒ zū
items.why: 也 belongs before 我租, as in 就是小说很普通，我也租。

items.note: Use 不光 or 不仅 to introduce the first point, then add a second point with 也, 还, or 而且. Learners often put 也 in the wrong position or reverse a verb-complement sequence.

items.phrase: 演出不光有趣而且值得观看
items.zh: 演出不光有趣，而且值得观看
items.en: The performance is not only interesting but also worth watching.
items.wrong: 演出不光有趣，而且观看值得
items.wrongPy: yǎn chū bù guāng yǒu qù ér qiě guān kàn zhí dé
items.why: 值得 must come before 观看, as in 演出不光有趣，而且值得观看。

items.note: Put 千万 directly before the action to express a strong urge or warning, often in prohibitions. Learners may move it after the verb; it must precede the verb phrase.

items.en: Be sure to take education seriously.
items.wrongPy: zhòng shì qiān wàn jiào yù
items.why: 千万 must come before the action; say 千万重视教育 to urge taking education seriously.

items.en: By all means, strengthen education.
items.wrongPy: jiā qiáng qiān wàn jiào yù
items.why: 千万 must come before the action; say 千万加强教育 to strongly urge strengthening education.

items.note: 更加 comes before a gradable predicate to show that something has a greater degree than before or than a comparison point. Learners may put it after the adjective; it must precede the predicate.

items.en: The mood is even more relaxed.
items.wrongPy: xīn qíng qīng sōng gèng jiā
items.why: 更加 must precede the adjective; say 心情更加轻松.

items.en: This result is even more interesting.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge jié guǒ yǒu qù gèng jiā
items.why: 更加 must precede the adjective; say 这个结果更加有趣.

items.phrase: 期末到来了考生更加紧张
items.zh: 期末到来了，考生更加紧张。
items.en: The end of the term has arrived, and the candidates are even more nervous.
items.wrong: 期末到来了，考生紧张更加。
items.wrongPy: qī mò dào lái le kǎo shēng jǐn zhāng gèng jiā
items.why: 更加 must precede 紧张; say 期末到来了，考生更加紧张.

items.note: 光, 仅, and 仅仅 go before the phrase they restrict, such as a person, activity, or quantity. Learners may place them after the verb; move them before the focused phrase instead.
只好 comes before a verb phrase when someone accepts the remaining course because alternatives are unavailable. Learners may put it after the verb; place it before the action instead.

items.en: We have no choice but to accept the result.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men zhǐ hǎo jié guǒ jiē shòu
items.why: 只好 must come before 接受结果; say 我们只好接受结果.

items.note: Use 并不 or 并没有 before a predicate to firmly reject an expected claim. The common mistake is placing 并 after the negation; keep 并 directly before 不 or 没有.

items.en: This isn't correct at all.
items.wrongPy: bìng zhè bú zhèng què
items.why: 并 must come before 不, so the correct order is 这并不正确.

items.note: 而 links two parallel or contrasting descriptive phrases, with one phrase on each side. Learners often move 而 to the beginning or end; it belongs between the two descriptions.
Use 不是A，而是B to reject one interpretation and replace it with the intended one. Do not separate 而 from 是 or treat the two parts as unrelated alternatives.
由于 introduces the cause, usually a noun phrase or cause clause, and the result follows. Learners may put 由于 after the cause; keep it at the start of the cause phrase.

Use a number before a measure word, then a noun; choose the measure by what is counted. 棵 is for plants, 幅 for pictures, and 台 for machines. Learners often choose a measure by shape rather than noun type.

就是说 introduces an explanation that restates or clarifies what came before. Put the complete expression before the explanation. Learners may reverse its parts or confuse this fixed connector with the separate words 就是 and 说.
难道 introduces a rhetorical challenge, and 吗 closes the question. Keep the proposition in ordinary sentence order after 难道. Learners often move 不 away from the verb or adjective it negates.

随着 introduces a developing circumstance that accompanies the main clause. Put the circumstance after 随着 and the resulting situation in the following clause. Learners often misplace 也 or put 了 before the word it completes.

Use a number, then a size adjective, then the measure word, and optionally the noun. The size describes the measured unit, as in 两大项任务. Learners often put the measure word before the size adjective; keep 大 before 项 here.

Use this pattern to state a total ratio: the quantity is the baseline quantity multiplied by a number. The multiplier goes after 的 and before 倍. Learners may reverse those two parts, confusing the stated ratio with an incorrect construction.

各位 is a respectful way to address or refer to a group, and it comes before the audience noun. 都 can then indicate that the statement applies to everyone in that group. Learners sometimes place 都 inside the audience noun phrase; put it before the verb instead.

于是 connects a preceding situation with a following event or result, and it normally introduces the second clause. Learners may put the second clause's subject after its verb; keep the subject before the predicate, as in 于是乘客换乘.

Use 尽管 ... 但是/可是 ... to concede a real circumstance before stating a contrasting result. The first clause supplies the fact; the second gives the outcome. Do not place 但是 inside the first clause or scramble the predicate.

Use <requirement>，否则 + <consequence> to state what happens if the requirement is not met. 否则 introduces the consequence, not the requirement; learners often reverse the order or omit a negative the consequence needs.
恐怕 introduces a cautious prediction or a concerned, often tactful statement. Put the proposition after 恐怕; learners may misplace 恐怕 or move adverbs such as 很 and 也 away from the words they modify.
不得不 + verb phrase expresses having no choice but to do something, often with reluctance. Keep 不得不 together before the action; learners often omit or add one 不 and accidentally change the meaning.

items.en: Staff have to work overtime.
items.wrongPy: rén yuán bú bù dé jiā bān
items.why: 不不得 is not the compelled-action pattern; the correct phrase is 人员不得不加班。

items.en: He has no choice but to go on a business trip early.
items.wrongPy: tā bù dé bù chū chāi tí qián
items.why: 提前 must precede 出差 here; the correct phrase is 他不得不提前出差。

items.en: We have no choice but to work.
items.wrongPy: wǒ men bù dé gàn huór
items.why: 不得 means an action is prohibited, not compelled; the correct phrase is 我们不得不干活儿。

items.note: Use 选 + person + 为/当 + role to say someone is selected for a role; the choice of verb and role marker must fit. Learners often put 为 or 当 before the selected person. These examples do not show 收, so do not assume it works in the same pattern.

items.en: The teachers and students select her as team captain.
items.wrongPy: shī shēng wèi xuǎn tā duì zhǎng
items.why: 为 is misplaced before 选; the correct order is 师生选她为队长。

items.en: The small group selects him as team captain.
items.wrongPy: xiǎo zǔ xuǎn dāng tā duì zhǎng
items.why: 当 must follow the selected person; the correct order is 小组选他当队长。

items.en: The teachers and students chose him as captain.
items.wrongPy: shī shēng xuǎn wèi tā duì zhǎng
items.why: 为 cannot come before the selected person here; the correct order is 师生选他为队长。

items.note: 不管 or 不论 introduces alternatives, and 都 or 也 comes before the predicate to show that the result holds across them. Learners often place 都 after the verb or before the subject. Keep the alternative clause and result clause distinct.

For an approximate round number, place 来 after the number and before the measure word, as in 十来个. Learners may omit the measure word or put 来 after it. This pattern is not freely used after every numeral.

items.en: About ten children won awards.
items.wrongPy: shí lái ér tóng huò jiǎng
items.why: 个 is required between 来 and 儿童; the correct form is 十来个儿童获奖。

items.note: 无日无夜 is a fixed four-character expression meaning “day and night.” Use it to describe something continuing at all times. Learners may mistakenly omit one 无; the paired form needs both 无 characters.

Put 将 or 将要 before a verb phrase to describe a prospective event, often in relatively formal language. This is a statement about what will happen, not what someone wants. A common mistake is placing 将要 after the verb phrase; it belongs before it.

items.en: The high-speed train is about to arrive.
items.wrongPy: dòng chē dào lái jiāng yào
items.why: 将要 must come before the verb phrase; the correct order is 动车将要到来.

items.en: The organization will launch a product.
items.wrongPy: dān wèi tuī chū shāng pǐn jiāng
items.why: 将 must precede 推出商品, not follow it; the correct order is 单位将推出商品.

items.note: 确实 comes before the predicate to confirm that something is genuinely the case. It can modify an adjective or a verb phrase. Learners may put a degree word such as 很 after the adjective; 很 belongs before it.

items.en: The road is indeed dangerous.
items.wrongPy: dào lù què shí wēi xiǎn hěn
items.why: 很 must come before 危险, not after it.

items.note: 为了 introduces a purpose, and 而 links that purpose to the action taken toward it. The pattern expresses intention, not necessarily success. Learners may place 而 after the action; it belongs between the purpose and the action.

items.en: Gather together to celebrate.
items.wrongPy: wèi le ér qìng zhù jù
items.why: 而 must follow the purpose 庆祝 and precede the action 聚.

items.note: 之 is a formal linker, and 之中 means “among” or “inside” the preceding noun phrase. It is not a freely interchangeable version of 的. Learners may reverse 之中; in these phrases, 中 follows 之.

Use 一方面 before the first consideration and 另一方面 before the second, whether the clauses are full sentences or short descriptions. The points may complement or compete with each other. Learners often omit or misplace one of the paired markers.

偶尔 goes before a verb phrase to say that an event happens sometimes, but not regularly. It can also precede 有 in an existential phrase. Learners often place it after the verb; do not confuse it with 偶然, which means accidental.

然而 introduces a contrary fact and usually begins the second clause; it is relatively common in written discourse. It links two clauses rather than serving as a sentence-final particle. Learners often put it in the wrong position or disrupt the word order within the second clause.

甚至 introduces a further point that is stronger or more surprising than the earlier one. It comes before that point, which may be a phrase or a full clause. Learners often put 甚至 after the point it is meant to introduce.

竟然 is an adverb placed before the predicate to show that an outcome is surprising or contrary to expectation. It can precede a verb or an adjective phrase. Learners often put it after the predicate; keep it before the whole predicate, while placing 很 or 不 within that predicate when needed.

For a fraction, put the denominator first, then 分之, then the numerator. The pattern is the reverse of how English usually says a fraction. Learners often switch the numerator and denominator; 三分之一 is one third, not three over one.

items.en: One third is here.
items.wrongPy: yì fēn zhī sān zài zhè
items.why: This puts the numerator before the denominator and means three over one, not one third; say 三分之一在这.

items.en: Two thirds are there.
items.wrongPy: èr fēn zhī sān zài nà
items.why: This means three over two, not two thirds; say 三分之二在那.

items.note: 本来 comes before a predicate to describe an original state or an expectation, often before circumstances changed. It can also begin the sentence. Learners may place it between a location and its verb; keep it before the predicate, and keep 在 before the location.

A number or fraction comes before 盒, 屋子, or 桌子, and the contents follow that container word. This describes a quantity held in a container or occupying a space. Learners often put the contents before the container; keep the measure phrase together before the contents.

items.en: Half a roomful of flowers smells good.
items.wrongPy: bàn xiān huā wū zi hěn xiāng
items.why: 鲜花 cannot come between the quantity and 屋子; say 半屋子鲜花很香.

items.note: Use formal 已 before the predicate to state that a situation has already been reached. It is common in concise or written Chinese. Learners often put 已 after the verb or object; unlike English “already,” it does not normally sit at the sentence end.

者 can turn certain verbs or adjectives into formal person-denoting nouns, as in 应聘者 and 管理者. Use established formations rather than attaching it freely to any word. Learners may place 者 before its base; it belongs after the compatible word.

稍 and 稍微 indicate a slight degree or a small adjustment and normally come before the predicate they modify. Use them with a gradable predicate. Learners often move them after the verb or its 了, where they do not form a grammatical degree expression.

加上 introduces an additional contributing cause, and the result follows the listed causes. Use it with a cause after it, rather than leaving 加上 without a complement. Learners may confuse the added cause with the result.

Use 跟 + comparison target + 相比 to name the baseline before stating the comparison. This is useful when the reference point must be explicit. Learners often omit 相比 or put the target after the clause; no example phrases were supplied here.

Place 对于 + a person or thing before the comment to set its target or scope. Use it when discussing an attitude or topic in relation to something. Learners sometimes put 有 after its object: say 有意见, not 意见有.

items.en: As for the works, let's discuss them later.
items.wrongPy: duì yú zuò pǐn zài ba shuō
items.why: 吧 follows the suggestion 再说, so keep 再说吧 together after the target.

items.note: Use 无论 with open alternatives, then 都 or 也 before the predicate to show that the result holds either way. This is a formal pattern. Learners often put 都 after the predicate or before the subject instead of before the predicate.

此 is a formal way to say “this” and directly modifies the noun that follows it. Use it in formal or written expressions. Learners sometimes insert 的 between 此 and the noun; the pattern here is 此 + noun, without 的.

items.en: He points to this picture.
items.wrongPy: tā zhǐ cǐ de tú
items.why: 此 directly modifies 图 without 的, so say 他指此图.

items.en: This method really works.
items.wrongPy: cǐ zuò fǎ yǒu xiào zhēn zhèng
items.why: 真正 must come before 有效 here, so say 此做法真正有效.

items.note: Use the role phrase first, followed by a comma and the statement about the person in that capacity. Learners may reverse the role marker and role noun; keep them together in the stated order.

items.en: As a writer, he is very confident.
items.wrongPy: zuò jiā zuò wéi tā hěn zì xìn
items.why: The role marker must come before the role noun; the correct opening is 作为作家。

items.en: As a writer, he is very funny.
items.wrongPy: zuò jiā zuò wéi tā hěn yōu mò
items.why: The role marker must come before the role noun; the correct opening is 作为作家。

items.note: 啊 expresses surprise, while 嗯 acknowledges or agrees; their interpretation depends on context and intonation. Use them as discourse responses, usually before a clause. Learners may insert them inside a clause as if they were ordinary adverbs.

items.phrase: 等到夜晚他到底回信了
items.zh: 等到夜晚，他到底回信了。
items.en: By nightfall, he finally replied.
items.wrong: 等到夜晚，他回信到底了。
items.wrongPy: děng dào yè wǎn tā huí xìn dào dǐ le
items.why: 到底 must come before 回信 here, as in the original, not after it.

items.note: This pivot pattern makes the person after the praise or criticism verb the subject of the following action: the person is praised or criticized for doing it. Keep that person before the action; learners often put the person after it.

items.en: The tour guide praised him by name.
items.wrongPy: dǎo yóu tā diǎn míng biǎo yáng
items.why: The person being praised must follow the praise verb, not come before it; the correct order is 导游点名表扬他。

items.note: Use 各 before a group or place noun, or before a measure word and noun, to mean each relevant member or unit. It commonly appears with 都. A common mistake is putting the measure word after the noun; keep the order 各个演员, not 各演员个.

items.en: Each actor performs in plays.
items.wrongPy: gè yǎn yuán gè dōu yǎn huà jù
items.why: The measure word 个 must precede 演员, so the correct phrase is 各个演员.

items.en: Every gathering is pleasant.
items.wrongPy: gè jù huì gè dōu hěn yú kuài
items.why: 个 must come before 聚会 after 各; the correct order is 各个聚会.

items.note: Put 得了 or 不了 after a verb to say whether someone can manage or complete an action. Here 了 is pronounced liǎo. Learners may confuse this complement with the ordinary completed-action marker 了 and place it after the verb incorrectly.

items.en: I can handle the pressure.
items.wrongPy: yā lì wǒ shòu bu liǎo
items.why: 不了 means the speaker cannot handle the pressure; the intended positive meaning requires 得了.

items.note: 怎么也不 or 怎么都不 describes repeated attempts with no success or change. Keep 也 or 都 between 怎么 and the negation; learners often move the adverb after the verb, where it no longer fits this pattern.

items.en: No matter what, he just won't subscribe.
items.wrongPy: tā zěn me bú dìng yě
items.why: 也 belongs between 怎么 and 不, so the correct order is 他怎么也不订。

items.note: 与 connects two noun phrases, especially in formal writing. It belongs between the nouns, not inside the predicate. Learners sometimes move 与 next to a verb or put it between a noun and its related phrase, disrupting the sentence structure.

items.en: He and she are tied.
items.wrongPy: tā bìng liè yǔ tā
items.why: 与 must connect the two noun phrases, not follow 并列; the correct form is 他与她并列。

items.en: The mind is related to feelings.
items.wrongPy: xīn yǔ yǒu gǎn qíng guān xì
items.why: 有 must follow the coordinated subject; the correct form is 心与感情有关系。

items.note: Use a cause, then 使 or 让, then the person experiencing the result, followed by the verb phrase. The pattern describes a resulting feeling or action, not necessarily a command. A frequent mistake is putting the person after the verb phrase.

items.en: She makes me proud.
items.wrongPy: tā ràng jiāo ào wǒ
items.why: The person must follow 让 and precede the result; put 我 before 骄傲.

items.note: Place 差点儿 or 差一点儿 before the verb phrase to say something nearly happened, usually but not actually happening. Do not assume a version with 不 has the same meaning: negation can change the interpretation and requires separate attention.

items.en: Almost caught up.
items.wrongPy: gǎn shàng chà diǎnr
items.why: 差点儿 must come before the verb phrase; put it before 赶上.

items.note: Put 究竟 or 到底 before the question phrase to press for the actual answer. Keep the question intact; these words do not replace the question form, and learners often put 吗 inside the sentence or combine it with another question form.

items.en: Did you actually agree?
items.wrongPy: nǐ dào dǐ le ma dā ying
items.why: 吗 belongs after the whole predicate, so the correct question is 你到底答应了吗？

items.en: Is it scientific after all?
items.wrongPy: jiū jìng shì bú shì ma kē xué
items.why: 是不是 already forms the question, so the correct form is 究竟是不是科学？ without 吗。

items.en: Is this approach any good?
items.wrongPy: zhè ge zuò fǎ dào dǐ bù hǎo hǎo
items.why: The choice question repeats 好 around 不, so the correct form is 这个做法到底好不好？

items.note: Use 叫 or 让 before an agent to describe a colloquial passive, followed by a bounded verb phrase. This reports what happened to the subject; learners can mistake it for permission or a command. No example phrases were provided.

Subject + 与 + person + verb phrase is a formal way to show a co-participant or counterpart in an action or relationship. Put 与 and the person before the verb phrase. Learners may mistakenly place 与 after the verb.

items.en: I go sightseeing with him.
items.wrongPy: wǒ tā yǔ yóu wán
items.why: 与 and 他 belong before the verb phrase; say 我与他游玩。

items.en: I contact him.
items.wrongPy: wǒ lián xì yǔ tā
items.why: 与他 must precede the verb; say 我与他联系。

items.en: I find it inconvenient to discuss it with him.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bú biàn shāng liang yǔ tā
items.why: 与他 must precede the verb phrase; say 我不便与他商量。

items.en: He discusses the requirements with me.
items.wrongPy: tā wǒ yǔ shāng liang tiáo jiàn
items.why: 与我 belongs after the subject and before the verb; say 他与我商量条件。

items.note: 不怎么 + gradable predicate means “not particularly” or “not very,” expressing a limited degree rather than total negation. Put 不怎么 before the predicate. Learners may place it after the adjective, where it no longer forms this pattern.

items.en: Cigarettes don't smell particularly nice.
items.wrongPy: yān xiāng bù zěn me
items.why: 不怎么 must precede the predicate; say 烟不怎么香。

items.en: He isn’t very polite.
items.wrongPy: tā lǐ mào bù zěn me
items.why: 不怎么 must precede the predicate; say 他不怎么礼貌。

items.en: The method isn’t particularly standard.
items.wrongPy: zuò fǎ biāo zhǔn bù zěn me
items.why: 不怎么 must precede the predicate; say 做法不怎么标准。

items.en: This process is not particularly easy.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge guò chéng qīng sōng bù zěn me
items.why: 不怎么 must precede the predicate; say 这个过程不怎么轻松。

items.note: Put 敢 before a verb phrase to say the subject has the courage to act, not merely the ability. 敢于 is another form used in some phrases; learners often place 敢 after the verb or mistake it for ability.

items.en: Dare you play the instrument?
items.wrongPy: nǐ tán qín gǎn ma
items.why: 敢 must precede the verb phrase, not follow it; the correct question is 你敢弹琴吗？

items.en: Does he dare to play the piano again?
items.wrongPy: tā gǎn tán zài cì qín ma
items.why: 再次 must come before the verb phrase 弹琴; the correct question is 他敢再次弹琴吗？

items.note: Place a number and 趟 after a trip-related verb to count journeys or rounds of travel or checkups, not objects or distance. Learners often put the number after the counter or confuse 趟 with an event counter.
共 goes before a quantity to state the total amount under discussion. Use it when summing items, trips, or other quantities. Learners often put 共 after the number, but the pattern is 共 + quantity.

往往 comes before a consequence to describe a frequent or typical result when a condition recurs. It does not mean that the result happens every single time. Learners often move 往往 after the predicate, where it does not fit.

items.en: When there is a gathering, online friends are often all there.
items.wrongPy: yǒu jù huì wǎng yǒu wǎng wǎng zài dōu
items.why: 都 cannot follow 在 here; the correct order is 网友往往都在。

items.phrase: 条件不好收入往往下降
items.zh: 条件不好，收入往往下降。
items.en: When conditions are poor, income often falls.
items.wrong: 条件不好，收入下降往往。
items.wrongPy: tiáo jiàn bù hǎo shōu rù xià jiàng wǎng wǎng
items.why: 往往 must come before the consequence, not after 下降; say 收入往往下降。

items.note: 全 goes after a plural subject and before its predicate to say that every member does something. Use it when there are no exceptions. Learners often put 全 after the verb instead of before the predicate.

items.en: They all passed.
items.wrongPy: tā men tōng guò quán le
items.why: 全 belongs before the predicate, not after 通过; say 他们全通过了。

items.en: All the internet users passed the medical examination.
items.wrongPy: wǎng yǒu men tōng guò tǐ jiǎn quán le
items.why: 全 must precede the predicate, not follow 体检; say 网友们全通过体检了。

items.note: Put 却 after the subject to mark a contrast with an expectation or a preceding fact. It can connect contrasting clauses or appear within a clause. Learners often put 却 before the subject or place 都 after 很; here 都 comes before 很.

items.en: It is lively, but I’m still bored.
items.wrongPy: rè nao shì rè nao què wǒ wú liáo
items.why: 却 follows the subject 我, so the correct order is 热闹是热闹，我却无聊。

items.note: 再次 comes before a verb phrase to say that an event happens another time; it does not mean only a future repetition. Learners often put it after the verb or verb phrase. Keep it before the action, while aspect particles such as 了 stay in their usual positions.

而 links a first clause with a contrasting or parallel second clause. Put 而 at the start of the second clause, before its subject. Learners sometimes move 而 to the beginning of the sentence or place words in the second clause out of order.

items.en: The gathering is lively, whereas he is bored.
items.wrongPy: ér jù huì rè nao tā wú liáo
items.why: 而 introduces the second clause, so it belongs before 他, as in 聚会热闹，而他无聊。

items.phrase: 聚会很热闹而他很无聊
items.zh: 聚会很热闹，而他很无聊。
items.en: The party is lively, whereas he is bored.
items.wrong: 聚会很热闹，而很他无聊。
items.wrongPy: jù huì hěn rè nao ér hěn tā wú liáo
items.why: The subject 他 must precede 很无聊, as in 聚会很热闹，而他很无聊。

items.note: 等 follows one or more examples to show that a list is not complete; an optional category noun may follow 等. Learners often put 等 before the list or move 都 after the verb. In these examples, 都 comes before the predicate.

items.en: Parking, medical checkups, and so on are all here.
items.wrongPy: tíng chē tǐ jiǎn děng zài dōu zhè
items.why: 都 belongs before 在, so the correct phrase is 停车、体检等都在这。

items.en: I have documents, manuals, and more.
items.wrongPy: wén jiàn shuō míng shū děng wǒ yǒu dōu
items.why: 都 belongs before 有, as in 文件、说明书等我都有。

items.note: 才不 + verb phrase is an emphatic way to refuse or deny doing something. Use it to stress that the subject will not act; learners sometimes put 不 before 才, but 才 must come first in this pattern.

items.en: I’m not afraid of him at all.
items.wrongPy: cái wǒ bú pà tā
items.why: 才不 precedes the verb phrase, while the subject 我 must come first: 我才不怕他。

items.note: 还 can precede a predicate to mark an assessment as noteworthy or unexpected. In some contexts it instead means “still” or “also”; learners should not move it after the predicate, as it comes before the predicate here.

items.en: He’s still very excited.
items.wrongPy: tā hěn hái xīng fèn
items.why: 还 comes before the predicate 很兴奋, not between 很 and 兴奋.

items.en: The gathering is surprisingly lively.
items.wrongPy: jù huì rè nao hái zhēn
items.why: 还真 precedes the predicate 热闹; it cannot be placed after that predicate here.

items.en: The gathering is surprisingly lively.
items.wrongPy: jù huì hái zhēn gòu de rè nao
items.why: 的 belongs at the end of 够热闹的, not between 够 and 热闹.

items.note: 一……一…… pairs balanced or contrasting units, such as 前 and 后 or 轻 and 重. Use established pairs in the same order; learners may misplace the repeated 一 or move 都 inside its predicate.

items.en: They are one in front and one behind.
items.wrongPy: tā men qián yí hòu yī
items.why: The established pair is 一前一后, with 一 before each direction.

items.note: Use 一 + measure word + 比 + 一 + the same measure word + adjective to show that each successive instance has more of a quality than the one before. It is often emphatic, not a literal ranking. Keep 比 between the two matching units.

Repeated 有 can present two paired items or qualities, as in 有男有女, or link parallel statements. Use it to highlight that both sides are present; do not insert 也 inside the first 有 phrase or scramble the parallel word order.

items.en: There are both men and women at the gathering.
items.wrongPy: jù huì nán yǒu yǒu nǚ
items.why: The repeated 有 must precede each item; the correct phrase is 聚会有男有女。

items.en: There are documents as well as explanations.
items.wrongPy: yǒu yě wén jiàn yǒu shuō míng
items.why: 也 cannot split 有 from 文件; the correct phrase is 有文件也有说明。

items.note: Repeat each item around 是 to distinguish two matters: A is A, and B is B. This can emphasize that they should not be conflated. Keep 是 after the first mention of each item, rather than moving it to the end of that repeated phrase.

items.phrase: 聚会是聚会工作是工作
items.zh: 聚会是聚会，工作是工作。
items.en: A get-together is one thing, and work is another.
items.wrong: 聚会聚会是，工作是工作。
items.wrongPy: jù huì jù huì shì gōng zuò shì gōng zuò
items.why: 是 must come between the repeated 聚会; the correct sentence is 聚会是聚会，工作是工作。

items.phrase: 热闹是热闹辛苦是辛苦
items.zh: 热闹是热闹，辛苦是辛苦。
items.en: It's lively, all right, but it's also hard work.
items.wrong: 热闹热闹是，辛苦是辛苦。
items.wrongPy: rè nao rè nao shì xīn kǔ shì xīn kǔ
items.why: 是 must come between the repeated 热闹; the correct sentence is 热闹是热闹，辛苦是辛苦。

items.note: 够 + adjective + 的 expresses a notably high degree, often with an evaluative or emphatic tone. It describes how strong a quality is, not whether there is enough of something. Keep 的 after the adjective, not between 够 and the adjective.

items.en: This trip is quite hard.
items.wrongPy: zhè tàng gòu de xīn kǔ
items.why: 的 must follow 辛苦, not precede it; the correct phrase is 这趟够辛苦的。

items.en: The get-together is quite lively.
items.wrongPy: jù huì gòu de rè nao
items.why: 的 must follow 热闹, not precede it; the correct phrase is 聚会够热闹的。

items.en: This trip is quite lively.
items.wrongPy: zhè tàng gòu de rè nao
items.why: 的 must follow 热闹, not precede it; the correct phrase is 这趟够热闹的。

items.en: It’s quite relaxing here.
items.wrongPy: zhèr gòu de qīng sōng
items.why: 的 must follow 轻松, not precede it; the correct phrase is 这儿够轻松的。

items.en: The gathering is surprisingly lively.
items.wrongPy: jù huì hái zhēn gòu de rè nao
items.why: 的 must follow 热闹, not precede it; the correct phrase is 聚会还真够热闹的。

items.note: The pattern counts each unit that is actually available: keep one article if you can, and that one counts. Use the same measure word on both sides. Learners may treat it as a promise of future quantity; it does not guarantee more units will come.

items.en: Save each article you can; every one counts.
items.wrongPy: liú piān yí shì yì piān
items.why: 一 must directly precede its measure word 篇; the correct phrase is 留一篇是一篇。

items.en: Keep whatever one you can.
items.wrongPy: liú yí shì yí gè
items.why: The first 一 needs its measure word 个; say 留一个是一个。

items.note: Use 有什么好 + verb phrase + 的 to challenge the idea that an action or reaction is warranted. It can be rhetorical or a genuine question. Learners often move 好 after the verb; here 好 must come before the action.

items.en: What is there to envy?
items.wrongPy: yǒu shén me de hǎo xiàn mù
items.why: 好羡慕 must stay together, with 的 at the end; the correct phrase is 有什么好羡慕的？

items.en: What's there to misunderstand?
items.wrongPy: yǒu shén me de hǎo wù huì
items.why: 好误会 must stay together, with 的 at the end; the correct phrase is 有什么好误会的？

items.en: What is there to be nervous about?
items.wrongPy: yǒu shén me de hǎo jǐn zhāng
items.why: 好紧张 must stay together, with 的 at the end; the correct phrase is 有什么好紧张的？

items.note: This pattern tells someone to continue their own activity, often dismissing interference: verb + 你的 + 吧. Learners may put 你的 before the verb; the activity must be named first, then 你的.

items.en: Go ahead and take your pictures.
items.wrongPy: nǐ nǐ de pāi ba
items.why: 你的 follows the activity verb; the correct order is 你拍你的吧。

items.en: Go ahead and tidy up.
items.wrongPy: nǐ nǐ de shōu shi ba
items.why: 你的 follows the activity verb; the correct order is 你收拾你的吧。

items.note: This pattern says to comply with an instruction: 让 or 叫 + you + action, then you + 就 + the same action. Learners may negate the second action, which reverses the intended compliance; repeat it affirmatively.

items.en: If you’re told to take the picture, just take it.
items.wrongPy: ràng nǐ pāi nǐ jiù bù pāi
items.why: The second clause repeats the requested action affirmatively; 不拍 contradicts compliance, so use 让你拍，你就拍。

items.en: I told you to tidy up, so tidy up!
items.wrongPy: ràng nǐ shōu shi nǐ jiù bù shōu shi
items.why: The second clause repeats the requested action affirmatively; 不收拾 contradicts compliance, so use 让你收拾，你就收拾！

items.note: Use 怎么着也得 before a verb phrase to say that an action must happen whatever the circumstances. The 也 comes before 得, which expresses necessity. Learners often put 得 before 也; that reverses the fixed order and makes the construction wrong.

items.en: No matter what, we have to wait.
items.wrongPy: zěn me zhe de yě děng
items.why: 也 must come before 得 in this construction; the correct phrase is 怎么着也得等。

items.en: I have to get a checkup no matter what.
items.wrongPy: zěn me zhe de yě tǐ jiǎn
items.why: 也 must come before 得 in this construction; the correct phrase is 怎么着也得体检。

items.en: I have to pass no matter what.
items.wrongPy: zěn me zhe de yě tōng guò
items.why: 也 must come before 得 in this construction; the correct phrase is 怎么着也得通过。

items.note: Put the action before 也得, then repeat the action after 不 and again after 也得. This paired pattern says the action is compulsory either way. Learners may place 得 before 也; in this pattern, 也 must immediately precede 得.

items.en: We have to wait whether we want to or not.
items.wrongPy: děng de yě děng bù děng yě de děng
items.why: 也 must precede 得 in the first clause; the correct phrase is 等也得等，不等也得等。

items.note: Repeat a predicate around 就 to reluctantly accept a situation; with an adjective, add 点儿吧 to mean accepting it to a limited degree. Learners can misplace the repeated predicate, but it belongs after 就, not after 吧.

items.en: I guess it can be a little messy.
items.wrongPy: luàn jiù ba luàn diǎnr
items.why: The repeated predicate must follow 就 and precede 吧; the correct phrase is 乱就乱点儿吧。

items.en: If it’s tough, so be it.
items.wrongPy: xīn kǔ xīn kǔ jiù ba
items.why: The repeated predicate must follow 就 and precede 吧; the correct phrase is 辛苦就辛苦吧。

items.note: Repeat the same predicate on both sides of 是 to concede or acknowledge a point, often before adding a qualification. Learners may reverse the repeated predicate and 是; the first predicate must come before 是, and its repeat must come after it.

items.en: It is lively, that’s true.
items.wrongPy: rè nao rè nao shì
items.why: 是 must fall between the repeated predicates; the correct phrase is 热闹是热闹。

items.en: A rule is a rule.
items.wrongPy: guī dìng guī dìng shì
items.why: 是 must fall between the repeated predicates; the correct phrase is 规定是规定。

items.en: It is lively, but I’m still bored.
items.wrongPy: rè nao rè nao shì wǒ què wú liáo
items.why: 是 must fall between the repeated predicates; the correct phrase is 热闹是热闹，我却无聊。

items.note: Use 死了 after compatible emotional or descriptive predicates for a colloquial extreme degree; use 得厉害 after a suitable predicate for “intensely.” Learners often put 死了 before the predicate or confuse 得 with 的.

items.en: I’m incredibly excited.
items.wrongPy: sǐ le wǒ xīng fèn
items.why: 死了 follows 兴奋 in this pattern; placing it first gives the wrong word order.

items.en: I’m extremely excited.
items.wrongPy: wǒ sǐ le jī dòng
items.why: 死了 must follow 激动 here, not precede it.

items.en: It’s incredibly lively here.
items.wrongPy: zhèr sǐ le rè nao
items.why: 死了 follows 热闹 in this pattern, so this word order is wrong.

items.en: This trip was exhausting.
items.wrongPy: zhè tàng sǐ le xīn kǔ
items.why: 死了 must follow 辛苦 here, not come before it.

items.note: Use 首先 before the first action and 然后 or 其次 before the next one to mark sequence. Learners can wrongly place an object before its verb when rearranging a clause.

items.phrase: 首先收拾文件然后停车
items.zh: 首先收拾文件，然后停车
items.en: First organize the files, then park.
items.wrong: 首先文件收拾，然后停车
items.wrongPy: shǒu xiān wén jiàn shōu shi rán hòu tíng chē
items.why: 收拾 must come before its object 文件; the first clause has the wrong word order.

items.phrase: 首先收拾文件然后体检
items.zh: 首先收拾文件，然后体检。
items.en: First tidy up the documents, then get a checkup.
items.wrong: 首先文件收拾，然后体检。
items.wrongPy: shǒu xiān wén jiàn shōu shi rán hòu tǐ jiǎn
items.why: 收拾 must come before its object 文件; the first clause has the wrong word order.

items.note: Repeat a predicate around 是 to concede a point, then use 不过 or 就是 to introduce a limitation. Learners often place 也 after the verb 有 instead of before it.

items.phrase: 规定是规定不过也有缺点
items.zh: 规定是规定，不过也有缺点。
items.en: Rules are rules, though they have drawbacks.
items.wrong: 规定是规定，不过有也缺点。
items.wrongPy: guī dìng shì guī dìng bú guò yǒu yě quē diǎn
items.why: 也 belongs before 有, so 有也缺点 puts the adverb in the wrong position.

items.note: Use 好让 before an action that you want to make possible through the preceding action. Learners may omit 让, but 好 must lead into the purpose clause through 好让 in these phrases.

items.phrase: 我收拾文件好让他回信
items.zh: 我收拾文件，好让他回信。
items.en: I organize the files so he can reply.
items.wrongPy: wǒ shōu shi wén jiàn hǎo tā huí xìn
items.why: The purpose clause needs 让 before 他; without it, 好他回信 is not grammatical here.

items.note: Use 要是 for a condition and 否则 to introduce the alternative consequence; 就 may be omitted. Learners often place 否则 before the first consequence or put 不 in the wrong position.

items.phrase: 要是他在我收拾否则我等
items.zh: 要是他在，我收拾；否则我等
items.en: If he is here, I’ll tidy up; otherwise, I’ll wait.
items.wrong: 要是不他在，我收拾；否则我等
items.wrongPy: yào shi bù tā zài wǒ shōu shi fǒu zé wǒ děng
items.why: 不 belongs before 在, not 他; the given condition is 要是他在.

items.note: Put 百分之 before the full number to express a percentage. The number must follow it directly; learners often reverse the order or separate the number from the marker.

items.en: Five percent is enough too.
items.wrongPy: wǔ bǎi fēn zhī yě gòu
items.why: The number must follow 百分之; the given phrase is 百分之五也够.

items.en: Ten percent is not enough.
items.wrongPy: bǎi fēn zhī bù shí gòu
items.why: 不 cannot split 百分之 from its number; the given phrase is 百分之十不够.

items.en: Twenty percent is enough too.
items.wrongPy: bǎi fēn zhī yě èr shí gòu
items.why: 也 cannot split 百分之 from the number; the given phrase is 百分之二十也够.

items.note: 不 + verb phrase introduces a condition treated as absent, and 也 marks the result that still holds. Learners often put 也 before 不 or use 不 directly with 有.
For decimals, say the whole-number digits, then 点, then read each fractional digit separately. Learners often move 点 or put the fractional digits before it.

items.en: This number is 2.5.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge shù shì èr wǔ diǎn
items.why: 点 must come before the fractional digit; the given decimal is 这个数是二点五.

items.en: The current number is 3.5.
items.wrongPy: xiàn yǒu shù zì shì sān wǔ diǎn
items.why: 点 must come before the fractional digit; the given decimal is现有数字是三点五.

items.en: This number is 3.5.
items.wrongPy: zhè ge shù zì shì wǔ sān diǎn
items.why: 点 must come before the fractional digit; the given decimal is这个数字是三点五.

items.note: Use 把 plus a known object and a suitable result or completion verb followed by 了 to present a bounded disposal event. Learners often put 了 before the verb; here it belongs after the completed verb phrase.

items.en: I got the fire started.
items.wrongPy: wǒ bǎ huǒ zhe nòng le
items.why: The resultative verb is 弄着, not 着弄; keep the verb and result in that order.

items.en: He broke the alarm clock.
items.wrongPy: tā bǎ nào zhōng pò dǎ le
items.why: The resultative verb is 打破, not 破打; keep the verb before its result.

items.note: 说不定 comes before a complete proposition to present it as a possible, uncertain outcome. Keep the proposition’s normal word order; learners sometimes rearrange its subject, verb, or object after 说不定.

items.en: Maybe it’s tasty.
items.wrongPy: shuō bu dìng xiān hěn
items.why: 很 precedes the adjective 鲜, as in 说不定很鲜.

items.en: Maybe he will take part in the assembly too.
items.wrongPy: shuō bu dìng yě tā cān yù dà huì
items.why: 也 belongs after the subject 他 and before 参与, as in 他也参与大会.

items.note: 有的是 + noun is an emphatic way to say there is plenty of something; use it for abundance, not merely an unspecified subset. Keep 的 between 是 and the noun. Learners may confuse 有的是 with 有的, which means “some.”

items.en: There are plenty of snacks.
items.wrongPy: yǒu de shì gè diǎn xin
items.why: 个 makes 点心 singular here, contradicting abundance; say 有的是点心。

items.en: There are plenty of trees in the forest.
items.wrongPy: sēn lín shì yǒu de shì shù
items.why: The extra 是 breaks 有的是; say 森林有的是树。

items.note: Use 一脸 or 一手 before a following expression to describe a face covered with a look or substance, or a hand associated with something. It is a conventional surface or whole-hand pattern; learners often put 一脸 or 一手 after the expression.

items.en: She has a disappointed look on her face.
items.wrongPy: tā shī wàng yì liǎn
items.why: The measure expression must come before the description; the correct phrase is 她一脸失望。

items.en: She has a good hand of cards.
items.wrongPy: tā hǎo pái yì shǒu
items.why: 一手 must precede 好牌 in this pattern; the correct phrase is 她一手好牌。

items.en: The passerby has a face covered in sweat.
items.wrongPy: lù rén hàn shuǐ yì liǎn
items.why: 一脸 must precede the substance covering the face; the correct phrase is 路人一脸汗水。

items.en: He has steamed buns in one hand and yogurt in the other.
items.wrongPy: tā mán tou yì shǒu suān nǎi yì shǒu
items.why: 一手 must precede the item in each clause; the correct phrase is 他一手馒头，一手酸奶。

items.note: Place the number and 场 after a verb to count bounded events such as competitions or matches. 场 counts events, not participants or objects; learners often reverse the number and counter or substitute a counter for trips.

items.en: He went through two competitions.
items.wrongPy: tā jīng lì le chǎng liǎng jìng zhēng
items.why: 两 must precede 场 in the event count; the correct sentence is 他经历了两场竞争。

items.en: He watched three final matches in a row.
items.wrongPy: tā lián kàn le chǎng sān jué sài
items.why: 三 must precede 场 in the event count; the correct sentence is 他连看了三场决赛。

items.note: Use 把 with an object that is already known, followed by a manner phrase and then the verb, when describing a bounded action that affects that object. Do not treat every 把 sentence as this pattern: the manner phrase goes before the verb, not after it.

items.en: Put the cover on.
items.wrongPy: bǎ tào ba tào shàng
items.why: 吧 closes the suggestion; keep it after the verb, as in 把套套上吧。

items.en: He gently wiped his leather shoes.
items.wrongPy: tā bǎ pí xié cā qīng qīng le
items.why: The manner adverb precedes 擦, so the correct order is 他把皮鞋轻轻擦了。

items.note: 老 comes directly before a predicate to describe repeated or persistent behavior, often with a sense of annoyance. Learners sometimes place 老 after the verb or object, but it must precede the predicate.

items.en: He always misunderstands me.
items.wrongPy: tā wù huì lǎo wǒ
items.why: 老 must precede the predicate 误会, not its object 我; say 他老误会我。

items.en: Online friends always misunderstand him.
items.wrongPy: wǎng yǒu wù huì lǎo tā
items.why: 老 belongs before 误会, not after it; the correct phrase is 网友老误会他。

items.en: He always misunderstands his online friends.
items.wrongPy: tā wù huì wǎng yǒu lǎo
items.why: 老 must precede the predicate 误会; the correct order is 他老误会网友。

items.en: He keeps finding fault with his wife.
items.wrongPy: tā lǎo tiāo tài tai le máo bìng
items.why: 了 cannot split 太太的毛病; the correct phrase keeps 的 together with its noun phrase.
